NEWS FROM THE BOARDNEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners November 2024 Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner ADA COUNTY ELECTIONS MAKES NATIONAL NEWS WITH AWARD-WINNING BALLOT VERIFIER The November 2024 General Election was one of the most closely watched elections in U.S. history. In Ada County we had a record number of people voting – 271,186 at final count. That’s 79% of the 349,361 registered Ada County voters. Ada County Elections made national news with the Ballot Veri ier which was profiled in a New York Times article. The ballot verifier system allows anyone to view cast ballots sorted by precinct, contest or candidate while protecting voter privacy. The system greatly enhances transparency and public trust in how elections are administered in Ada County. Ada County Clerk Trent Tripple and the Ada County Elections team won national recognition for the ballot verifier and were honored for their groundbreaking work by the Ada County Commissioners. Interested in learning more: https://adacounty.id.gov/elections/ ballot-verifier-info/

CONGRATULATIONS TO OUR ADA COUNTY TREASURER ELIZABETH MAHN ON BEING AWARDED THE EXCELLENCE IN FINANCE AWARD BY THE IDAHO BUSINESS REVIEW “With more than two decades of experience, Mahn has become a pivotal figure in administering complex property tax legislation and overseeing public funds in Idaho’s most populous county.” Ada County Treasurer Elizabeth Mahn received the Excellence in Finance Award in November from the Idaho Business Review. Mahn has been Ada County’s Treasurer since 2018. Her work implementing the Idaho Legislature’s House Bill 292 is just the latest in Mahn’s achievements implementing and administering Idaho’s tax laws. HB 292 provided roughly $99 million in property tax relief to Ada County property owners. When you receive your property tax bill check out the easy-to-understand outline of where your money goes and how much you saved on property taxes due to HB292. Mahn has a law degree (Juris Doctor) from the University of Idaho as well as a Bachelor of Science degree in Business with a focus on accounting. “My personal philosophy is rooted in accountability and dependability and following through with commitments to my family, peers, colleagues and community.” Elizabeth Mahn, Ada County Treasurer In the Idaho Business Review article Seth Grigg, the Executive Director of the Idaho Association of Counties said, “Elizabeth’s deep understanding of the intricacies of property tax law, commitment to working with policy makers to find solutions to address rising property taxes in Idaho and her dedication to public service were instrumental in ensuring that the program was administratively feasible.” You can read the full article here: https://idahobusinessreview.com/2024/11/21/ excellence-in-finance-elizabeth-mahn-ada-county/ Pictured Left-Right: Guisela Crespo Kuba, Financial Specialist; Amanda Cline, and Tim Cline, Chief Deputy; Mercy Clarkson, Banking Analyst; Brian Clarkson, Briar Seegmiller, Financial Specialist; Elizabeth Mahn, Ada County Treasurer; Rob Brown, Finance and Banking Manager; Dan Pearson, and Amanda Pearson, Financial Analyst 4

ROB BROWN RECOGNIZED FOR NATIONAL CERTIFICATION ACHIEVEMENT Rob Brown, Banking and Finance Manager with the Ada County Treasurer’s Office, has been awarded the Advanced Certified Public Funds Investment Manager (ACPFIM) Certification from the Association of Public Treasurers of the United States and Canada (APT US&C). The nationally recognized ACPFIM program is designed to provide treasury professionals with the confidence and knowledge to better manage investments on behalf of their municipalities and clients. The ACPFIM is awarded to approximately 50 individuals annually. To achieve certification of the ACPFIM individuals must demonstrate continued investment education training every five years. To qualify for the ACPFIM, individuals must first earn the CPFIM certification by completing a comprehensive training program and successfully passing an exam on training objectives components: identifying and understanding investment options; how and where to buy investments; establishing internal controls and developing procedures; identifying and mitigating risk in a portfolio; quantifying and reporting safety measures; understanding liquidity needs and yield calculations; managing and forecasting investments; and implementing and monitoring strategy. To earn the ACPFIM individuals must further their instruction on investment analysis, strategy, and implementation and successfully pass the advanced training exam. Congratulations, Rob!! Pictured Left-Right Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Banking and Finance Manager Rob Brown, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson The Ada County Treasurer’s Office is proud to have three outstanding leaders who are nationally certified. Pictured Left-Right: Banking and Finance Manager Rob Brown, Ada County Treasurer Elizabeth Mahn, and Chief Deputy Treasurer Tim Cline 5

LEADERSHIP MERIDIAN GOVERNMENT DAY Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck Speaks to Current and Future Leaders Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck was honored to be invited to speak to the 2024 Leadership Meridian Government Day attendees in November. More than thirty people were on hand for the lunch event. Chairman Beck outlined the importance of learning the geography, demographics, and predicted growth for all of Ada County. “If you own a business or want to expand your business, it’s important to know where the community is growing,” said Chairman Beck. Thank you to Leadership Meridian and Sean Evans with the Meridian Chamber of Commerce for coordinating the annual event. 6 BOISE KUNA MERIDIAN GARDEN CITY EAGLE STAR CANYON COUNTY BOISE COUNTY ELMORE COUNTY OWYHEE COUNTY GEM COUNTY §¨¦ §¨¦ UNINCORPORTED ADA COUNTY Federal Land (19,920) (36,300) (13,380) (250,060) (142,830) (31,490) (63,610) (2024 COMPASS Population Estimates) Ada County Ada County is the largest county by population in Idaho, home to approximately 27% of the state’s population. Ada County is more than 1000 square miles of high desert beauty, peppered with foothills and a glistening river that winds through urban and rural landscapes. Ada County includes Idaho’s capital city, Boise, and is home to ÿve other distinct municipalities – Star, Eagle, Meridian, Garden City and Kuna. The county is known for a rich agricultural heritage and open spaces for recreation. Ada County’s Barber Park is the put-in location for one of the region’s most popular activities – the Boise River Float. Ada County is also the state’s commerce and industry hub. Expo Idaho in Ada County hosts the annual Western Idaho Fair, one of the biggest and most popular events each year in Southwest Idaho. Protecting Ada County’s unique character now and in the years to come remains paramount for leaders across the county. Federal Land (2024 COMPASS Population Estimates)

DEMOGRAPHIC INFORMATION FROM THE LEADERSHIP MERIDIAN EVENT Meridian is the fastest growing city in Ada County by number of residents with 4,210 newcomers arriving between 2023 and 2024. The fastest growing city by percent was Star which saw a 13.7% increase in population during the same time period. Meridian and Star were also the fastest growing cities in Ada County from 2020 – 2024. Meridian’s population is now more than 145-thousand people. For context – Meridian’s population was just over 36,000 in the year 2000. In the year 2000 Star’s population was 2,000 people. Now it’s roughly 20,000. That’s a lot of change in 24 years! Meridian 2000 2024 Star, Idaho 2000 2024 36,000 145,000 2,000 20,000 Local Government SnapshotLocal Government Snapshot Every Idaho resident lives in a county. Each county has a county seat. Ada County’s County Seat is Boise. Counties serve as an administrative arm of the state. Counties carry out the laws and regulations put in place by the State Legislature. County Officials include: Commissioners (3) Clerk Assessor Treasurer Prosecuting Attorney Coroner Sheriff Among their many mandated functions, counties are required to have a jail, conduct elections, value all property, collect taxes for other entities, and perform solid waste collection and disposal. Some Well Known Ada County Facilities: Expo Idaho – Home of the Western Idaho Fair The Ada County Landfill Barber Park Ada County Victim Services Center The Bridge COUNTY www.adacounty.id.gov CITIES Cities are voluntarily organized and may be incorporated under the general laws of the state. Cities are local units which for the most part perform functions that are exclusively local. Think of Parks, Public Works, Police, Fire, just to name a few. Ada County has six cities: STAR, EAGLE, MERIDIAN, GARDEN CITY, BOISE AND KUNA Most Idaho cities operate under a Mayor/Council form of government, but all cities have the option to adopt a council/city manager plan. TAXING DISTRICTS Smaller local units of government that include, but are not limited to, cities, school districts, irrigation districts, fire protection districts, cemetery districts, and community college districts. 9 WILLIAM BROWNFIELD RECOGNIZED FOR 20 YEARS OF OUTSTANDING SERVICE Twenty years flies by when you’re working hard and making a difference. Congratulations to William Brownfield for twenty years of service to Ada County. William started his career with the Ada County DMV in October of 2004, at the Chinden DMV office. He spent his first week of training at the Barrister office back when Motor Vehicles was located there. Early on, William showed a propensity to learn fast and was tasked with reviewing titles the staff processed for accuracy. In 2005 William was made a trainer and was tasked with training the new hires - some of these people are the very people who hold management positions today. William moved to the Meridian DMV office in 2006, then in 2009 an opportunity came for William to return to Chinden, during this time He was also asked to become a back-up person for the DMV accountant due to his previous background in financial services and his attention to detail. William decided to go for his MBA on the side while working at the DMV and completed it in four months. During that time William’s lunches consisted of his nose in a book or two, possibly three. Pictured Left-Right Clayton Hall, DMV Division Manager William Brownfield, DMV Branch Supervisor Linda Gram, DMV Branch Manager William got promoted to lead clerk at Chinden in early 2020, shortly after he was asked to go to the Franklin office, after a short time there, he was promoted to Branch Supervisor, the role he still holds today. William is a number cruncher, if you ask him how many Fridays, he has left to get to his rule of 90, he could probably tell you the exact amount. We are grateful to have William as a part of our Ada County DMV Team, he is a great asset to Ada County as well as the public we serve. ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks and waterways, public defense, indigent services, juvenile court, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County www.adacounty.id.gov/ 9

ADA COUNTY EMPLOYEES HAVE BIG HEARTS “Rake Up” Teams burn major calories helping community members dispose of fall leaves Approximately fifty Ada County employees and their family members volunteered to do something incredibly meaningful in late November - they raked up and bagged mountains of leaves from yards throughout Ada County. One home in Kuna required 100 bags! Team Ada County was made up of employees from virtually every office and department of the county. For many Ada County employee volunteers, it was a family affair with spouses, children, and incredibly cute dogs pitching in to help. Thank you to all the folks who pitched in, and a big thanks to our team captains Chief Operating Officer (COO) Steve Rutherford (Cooper’s dad), and Trial Court Administrator (TCA) Sandra Barrios. See you next year! 10
